Ava (Mktg): OK team — quick sync. I drafted a compact "pocket guide" we can use for the launch blog, webinar one-pager, and sales snippets. Goal: a single tight latency vs cost story that maps to 3 audience playbooks. Thoughts?
Ravi (Prod): love the idea. can you paste the 3 playbooks here? want to make sure they map to model/infra choices.
Ava (Mktg): sure — rough: 1) Low-latency consumer features (prioritize small seqs, fast-path models) 2) Cost-sensitive high-throughput (batching, quantized model variants) 3) Regulated/enterprise (private deployment, SLA-backed Dedicated). Each has 1-line claim, 1 chart ask, and 2 inbound hooks.
Marta (Growth): for inbound hooks, we should make CTA variants: "Estimate your per-request cost", "See latency at 99th percentile", and "Request an on-prem trial". Different campaign landing pages.
Jon (Design): for the chart ask — recommend a 3-panel compact viz: left = median latency vs token length (lines per model family), middle = cost per 1k tokens (bar chart with quantized vs FP16), right = throughput (reqs/sec) for Dedicated configs. Clean legend, small annotations. I can mock by tomorrow.
Sam (Ops): FYI the Dedicated numbers need footnote: peak throughput depends on pooling and burst settings. suggest we add an asterisk and link to docs. Also add a fallback row for model-variant behavior.
Ravi (Prod): calling out routing policy in the copy is important — e.g., "auto-fallback to compatible model variant when capacity constrained". That's resonance for platform buyers.
Ava (Mktg): agreed. Draft copy for the pocket guide (short): "Optimize for your tradeoff: pick the low-latency model for instant UX, enable quantized pools for cost at scale, or deploy Private for compliance and SLAs. Redwood gives one API, three controls." Feedback?
Marta (Growth): tighten the lead: "Latency where it matters. Cost where it counts." Then 3 bullets linking to quick calculators. Also we should A/B test hero claim vs numbers-first approach.
Jon (Design): quick note on accessibility — the 3-panel needs high contrast and simplified axes. For the webinar slides, we can animate a sweep showing how batching reduces cost but increases median latency — very intuitive.
Sam (Ops): can we add a tiny snippet for sales engineers: command to repro perf: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -d '{"model":"r-infer-6B","input":"<sample>"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'``` plus note about enabling prefix cache? that'll help field demos.
Ava (Mktg): perfect. Action items: Jon — 1st mock of 3-panel + slide animation by EOD tomorrow. Sam/Ravi — verify Dedicated numbers and produce the tiny curl/snippets + a 1-paragraph SRE note for footnote. Marta — set up A/B test matrix and landing page CTAs. I'll stitch copy and run a final pass.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: assets/marketing/pocket-guide-v1 -> staging at 2026-04-02T18:00Z :white_check_mark:
Ava (Mktg): thanks! one more ask — make the pocket guide printable (single page) and also a 280-char tweet variant. Low-effort, high-leverage.
Marta (Growth): I'll draft the tweet. Suggest: "Latency where it matters. Cost where it counts. Redwood lets you optimize both — hosted, dedicated, or private. Try the pocket guide -> <shortlink>"
Ravi (Prod): minor nit: call out prefix cache and KV caching in one bullet. It sells the tech advantage without heavy detail.
Ava (Mktg): noted. I'll include that. Closing: we'll reconvene after Jon's mock. :thumbsup:
